intended_object: The second parallel arrow ∏_i P(X_i) → ∏_{(i,j)} P(X_i ×_B X_j) of the fork diagram in the equalizer sheaf condition (Stacks 00VM). It is induced by the second projections X_i ×_B X_j → X_j, for a type-valued presheaf P and a family of arrows π_i : X_i → B. Inferred from the docstring and the stacks tags on the neighbouring FirstObj/SecondObj.
explanation: The body is `Pi.lift fun _ => Pi.π _ _ ≫ P.map (pullback.snd _ _).op`. Since `pullback.snd : pullback (π i) (π j) ⟶ X j`, the omitted projection index is forced to be j. So the (i, j)-component is P(pr₂) ∘ proj_j : ∏ P(X_k) → P(X_i ×_B X_j), exactly the second map of the Stacks 00VM fork. The source and target (`FirstObj`, `SecondObj`) are the products over I and over I × I, as in Stacks; this handles families with duplicate arrows correctly. The lemmas `w` and `compatible_iff` (a family is compatible iff firstMap and secondMap agree on it) confirm the intended role. The generality is natural for this type-valued equalizer condition: presheaves of types, any w-small index type, and only pairwise pullbacks assumed. The presieve-indexed `Equalizer.Presieve.secondMap` in the same file is a related but distinct object when the family has duplicates, so it is not a more general version of this definition.
